rektion: etw. (Akk.) annehmen (ein Paket, ein Angebot, ein Geschenk); annehmen, dass … (= vermuten)
meaning_en: to accept, to take (receive); to assume
definition_de: etwas, das einem gegeben oder angeboten wird, nehmen (ein Paket / eine Einladung / einen Vorschlag annehmen); auch: vermuten (Ich nehme an, dass er krank ist.)
example_de: Weil mein Nachbar nicht zu Hause war, habe ich sein Paket angenommen.
example_en: Because my neighbour wasn't home, I took in his parcel.
visual_idea: Collocation 'ein Paket (für den Nachbarn) annehmen', a daily German routine: the courier hands over a big box at the apartment door and the woman in slippers takes it, while the neighbour's closed door shows whose parcel it is. Rejected: 'ein Angebot annehmen' (a handshake reads as 'begrüßen') and 'annehmen, dass …' (abstract).
image_prompt: the stairwell landing of an old German apartment building; a delivery man in a brown jacket hands a large plain brown cardboard box with no labels to a smiling woman in a grey cardigan and slippers standing in her open apartment door, she reaches out with both arms to take it; across the landing the closed wooden door of the neighbour's apartment with an empty doormat
negative_prompt: text, letters, watermark, signature, caption, blurry, extra fingers, deformed hands, cluttered background, multiple panels
video_prompt: on the landing of an old apartment building a delivery man rings at the neighbour's closed door, waits, then turns to a woman in a cardigan opening her own door; he hands her a large brown box and she takes it with both arms and nods; static camera
